subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the unintended public SDK export is removed, should OpenClaw accept this first-party external MXC sandbox plugin with the current native dependency graph and the MXC SDK 0.7.0 argv-carried config transport?
rationale: Automation can remove the stray SDK export, but only maintainers/secops can accept the new native sandbox dependency set, `node-pty` build allowance, packaged executor binaries, and process-list exposure boundary of `--config-base64`.

options.title: Accept after SDK export fix
options.body: Remove the unintended sandbox SDK export, then have an admin/secops owner approve the exact head dependency graph and accept the preview SDK argv boundary for this prerelease plugin.

options.title: Require transport mitigation
options.body: Keep the PR paused until the MXC SDK or plugin can pass the sandbox config through a non-argv transport with matching Windows proof.

options.title: Defer first-party MXC
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own MXC as a first-party sandbox plugin yet.

recommendation.title: Accept after SDK export fix
recommendation.body: Remove the unintended sandbox SDK export, then have an admin/secops owner approve the exact head dependency graph and accept the preview SDK argv boundary for this prerelease plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is currently assigned to `steipete`, and the remaining decision spans product acceptance plus secops routing rather than a code-only repair.
